about.title: Hi, I'm Hryhorii Kyrylchenko
about.description: .NET backend developer building ASP.NET Core Web APIs with clean architecture, secure endpoints and tested code.
about.content:
I'm a .NET backend developer focused on ASP.NET Core Web APIs: clean architecture, secure REST endpoints and code that is tested and easy to change. I'm currently a Trainee .NET Developer at EPAM Systems in the .NET Specialization program.

I came to software from law, logistics, sales and consulting. That background taught me to understand the business problem before writing code, to explain technical decisions to non-technical people, and to take ownership of results.

I studied software development at IT STEP Academy, starting in Ukraine and finishing remotely after moving to Poland. In my diploma project, Forja, I owned the backend: database design, architecture and all server-side functionality.

I'm based in Poznań and open to .NET developer roles where I can keep growing within a strong engineering team.

cookies.page_description: This policy explains how cookies are used on this site.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.p1: This Cookie Policy explains which cookies and similar technologies hryhoriikyrylchenko.dev (the "Site") uses. The Site uses only what is strictly necessary for the features you use, and nothing for analytics, advertising or tracking.

what-are.title: What are cookies?
what-are.p1: Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser. Local storage is a similar browser feature for saving settings on your device. Neither is sent to anyone other than this Site.

list.title: What the Site stores
list.p1: "translocoLang" (cookie): the language you chose with the language switcher. It is set only when you choose a language and expires after one year.
list.p2: "cookie_consent" (cookie): records that you closed the cookie notice, so it is not shown again. It expires after one year.
list.p3: "theme" (local storage): your light or dark theme setting. It stays until you clear your browser data.

consent.title: Why no consent is needed
consent.p1: All of the above are strictly necessary to provide features you ask for, such as keeping your language and theme, so under EU law they do not require your consent. The cookie notice informs you about them; closing it does not enable any additional cookies.

manage.title: How to manage cookies
manage.p1: You can view and delete cookies and local storage in your browser settings. If you do, the Site will use your browser language and default theme again, and the cookie notice will reappear.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: If the Site starts storing anything else, this policy will be updated first. Last updated: 14 November 2026.

privacy.page_description: This policy explains how this website processes data and protects user privacy.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.p1: This Privacy Policy explains how hryhoriikyrylchenko.dev (the "Site") handles information when you visit it. The Site is a static developer portfolio: it has no user accounts, contact forms, newsletters, analytics or advertising.

data_controller.title: Data controller
data_controller.p1: The controller of personal data processed in connection with the Site is Hryhorii Kyrylchenko, Poznań, Poland. You can reach me at contact@hryhoriikyrylchenko.dev.

hosting.title: Hosting and server logs
hosting.p1: The Site is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. When you visit the Site, GitHub logs your IP address for security purposes, together with technical details of the request such as the time and browser information.
hosting.p2: This processing is based on a legitimate interest in operating the Site securely and preventing abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). I do not have access to these logs and do not use them for tracking or profiling. GitHub may process this data in the United States; see the GitHub Privacy Statement for details and retention.
hosting.p3: The connection to the Site is encrypted (HTTPS).

correspondence.title: When you contact me
correspondence.p1: If you email me or message me through LinkedIn or GitHub, I process the data you send, such as your name, email address and message, only to reply to you and, where relevant, to discuss a job opportunity. The legal basis is my legitimate interest in answering inquiries and, for recruitment, steps taken at your request before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR).
correspondence.p2: I keep this correspondence only as long as needed for the conversation or recruitment process, and then delete it unless you ask me to keep it.

cookies_storage.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies_storage.p1: The Site uses only strictly necessary storage: a cookie with your chosen language ("translocoLang"), a cookie remembering that you closed the cookie notice ("cookie_consent") and a local storage entry with your theme ("theme").
cookies_storage.p2: They are not used for tracking or advertising and are not shared with anyone. The Cookie Policy describes each of them.

third_parties.title: Third-party services and links
third_parties.p1: The Site does not use analytics, advertising networks, tracking pixels, social media plugins or externally hosted fonts or scripts. All files, including the downloadable CV, are served from the Site itself.
third_parties.p2: The Site links to my GitHub and LinkedIn profiles. When you follow these links, the privacy policies of those services apply.

data_sharing.title: Data sharing
data_sharing.p1: I do not sell, rent or share personal data with third parties for marketing or any other purpose.

user_rights.title: Your rights
user_rights.p1: Under the GDPR you have the right to access your personal data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing and to object to processing based on legitimate interest. To exercise these rights, email contact@hryhoriikyrylchenko.dev. For server logs, you can also contact GitHub directly.
user_rights.p2: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. In Poland this is the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych, uodo.gov.pl).

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.p1: I may update this policy when the Site or the law changes. The current version is always published on this page with its date.

forja.title: Forja: Game Studio Platform
forja.short: Backend for an independent game studio's platform: game builds, player feedback and content. Team diploma project at IT STEP Academy; I owned the backend.

sections.overview: An independent game studio needed one place to publish game builds, collect player feedback and bug reports, and manage its internal content, instead of stitching together generic tools. Forja was built as a team diploma project at IT STEP Academy, with separate frontend, design and security roles. I owned the backend.
sections.features: Player feedback and bug reporting, management of game builds and assets, and an internal content management system for studio projects. The backend serves more than 40 dynamic UI pages.
sections.architecture: ASP.NET Core controllers and services over PostgreSQL with Entity Framework Core. Key decisions: Redis caching for frequently read data, which made data retrieval 40% faster; MinIO for S3-compatible object storage, so large build files stay out of the database and the platform is not tied to one cloud; Keycloak for authentication instead of a hand-written identity layer; and Swagger documentation plus the .NET Aspire dashboard, so the frontend team could integrate and debug without waiting on me.
sections.deployment: Every service runs in a Docker container and is orchestrated with .NET Aspire. Because storage is S3-compatible and identity is external, the same setup can run on AWS, Azure or a private cloud.
sections.results: I designed the database schema and the backend architecture and implemented all server-side functionality, delivering the complete backend in a three-month sprint in step with the frontend and security milestones.
sections.technologies: C#, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Keycloak, Docker, Swagger, .NET Aspire, Git.

personal-site.title: Personal Website: Full-Stack Portfolio & Blog
personal-site.short: Multilingual portfolio and blog with an admin panel: ASP.NET Core backend in Clean Architecture, Angular frontend, Docker on AWS and CI/CD with GitHub Actions.

sections.overview: I wanted a site I could keep updating myself: a portfolio, a blog and an admin panel for editing content and translations without redeploying. I designed and built it end to end and worked with a UX designer on the interface.
sections.features: Nine responsive pages, including About, a portfolio with detailed project pages, a blog and a contact form with email notifications. Content and translations are managed in the admin panel, with localization from JSON files and the database.
sections.architecture: The backend follows Domain-Driven Design and Clean Architecture and is organized in vertical slices. Each slice holds its own MediatR request, handler, validation and endpoint, with commands and queries separated (CQRS), so a feature can change without touching the others. Data lives in PostgreSQL through Entity Framework Core. The frontend is Angular, fully responsive and localized.
sections.deployment: Containerized with Docker and deployed to AWS. A GitHub Actions pipeline builds and deploys the app and runs database migrations and infrastructure provisioning automatically, which cut deployment time from 15 to 5 minutes.
sections.results: I built the whole platform: backend, frontend, database and deployment. I covered the backend with unit tests (xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions) and maintained the live site. The portfolio part now runs as a static version (this website), while the full-stack code remains available as a reference.
sections.technologies: C#, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, MediatR, PostgreSQL, Angular, TypeScript, Docker, AWS, GitHub Actions, xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions.

portfolio-static.title: Static Portfolio Site
portfolio-static.short: This website: a backend-free Angular SPA on GitHub Pages, with JSON-driven content and English/Polish localization.

sections.overview: A static rewrite of my full-stack personal site. The goal was to keep the portfolio online without paying for servers: there is no backend, and the whole site is served from GitHub Pages.
sections.features: Experience timeline, project case studies, skills, certifications, downloadable CV, light and dark themes, and English/Polish localization with the chosen language remembered in a cookie.
sections.architecture: Angular standalone components with a lazy-loaded case study page. Services join several JSON files on the client (experience, projects, skills, categories), reproducing what the original API did, so content is edited as data plus translation keys.
sections.deployment: GitHub Actions builds and deploys on every push to main. A post-build script copies the app shell to every known route, so deep links and refreshes return HTTP 200 while unknown URLs return a real 404.
sections.results: Hosting costs dropped to zero and the live site always matches the repository. New jobs and projects are added as JSON entries without code changes.
sections.technologies: Angular, TypeScript, RxJS, Transloco, SCSS, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages.
